title: Cohomology of the projective line and the trace
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an integer $r\geq1$, and a finite commutative $\mathbf Z/\ell^r\mathbf Z$-algebra $\Lambda$. On each site the coefficient ring sheaf is the constant sheaf associated to the finite discrete ring $\Lambda$; the Tate twists below need only be locally constant. Use the small pro-etale site and its ordinary derived category [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], derived tensor [def-weil-derived-tensor], and the exact inverse image and derived direct image with their adjunction [sk-def-sfb-finite-derived-functors]. For a scheme $T$ on which $\ell$ is invertible, put $\Lambda_{T,\mathrm{et}}(1)=\mu_{\ell^r,T}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/\ell^r}\Lambda_T$, and $\Lambda_{T,\mathrm{et}}(-1)=\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(\Lambda_{T,\mathrm{et}}(1),\Lambda_T)$ [def-asd-finite-etale-tate-sheaf]. Define $\Lambda_T(\pm1)=\nu_T^*\Lambda_{T,\mathrm{et}}(\pm1)$ using the etale/pro-etale comparison pullback [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback], and $K(1)=K\otimes_\Lambda^L\Lambda_T(1)$. The Chern class is the scalar-extended Kummer boundary, pulled through $\nu_T^*$; it is also the Cartier class composite of [sk-lem-geo-cartier]. Write $\mathbf P^1_S=\mathbf P(\{0,1\};S)$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. The line bundle $\mathcal O(1)$ is given on the standard charts by the degree-one transition $e_i=(x_i/x_j)e_j$ [def-pc-projective-space-twist]. A Noetherian scheme means one with a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings.

Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible and
$p:\mathbf P^1_S\to S$ the projection. The unit
$\Lambda_S\to Rp_*\Lambda_{\mathbf P^1_S}$ and the class
$c_1(\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1_S}(1))$ define an isomorphism

$$
\Lambda_S\oplus\Lambda_S(-1)[-2]
      \ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ Rp_*\Lambda_{\mathbf P^1_S}
      \quad\text{in }D(S_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda),   \qquad\text{(G2)}
$$

compatible with base change: for $g:S'\to S$ with $S'$ as in the lemma, the
base-change map $g^*Rp_*\Lambda\to Rp'_*\Lambda$ in
$D(S'_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ carries the pullback of (G2) to (G2) for $S'$.
Let

$$
\operatorname{Tr}_p:Rp_*\Lambda_{\mathbf P^1_S}(1)[2]\longrightarrow\Lambda_S
\qquad\text{(G3)}
$$

be the morphism in $D(S_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ given by the projection onto
the summand $\Lambda_S$ of the twist of (G2). Then $\operatorname{Tr}_p$ is
compatible with every Noetherian base change.

proof.text: Put $P=\mathbf P^1_S$ and $N=\ell^r$. The projection $p$ is proper by [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper], hence separated and of finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Finite type includes quasi-compactness [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and separated morphisms are quasi-separated [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated]. Also $P$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Thus all the ordinary etale proper-projection and comparison results used below apply, including after replacing $S$ by any Noetherian $S'$. By [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback], the etale twists are invertible locally free lines, their pullbacks are the corresponding twists, and these comparisons respect evaluation and tensor products. In particular twisting by $(1)[2]$ has inverse twisting by $(-1)[-2]$. Over $\operatorname{Spec}R\subset S$, the standard Proj charts [def-nagata-affine-proj] and affine fibre products [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] give $R[t]$, $R[s]$, where $t=x_1/x_0$, $s=x_0/x_1$ and $s=t^{-1}$ on the intersection: the degree-zero monomials after inverting $x_i$ are powers of $x_{1-i}/x_i$. The infinity section $D$ is empty on the $t$ chart and is $s=0$ on the $s$ chart. Its ideal has generators $1,s$; multiplication by $s$ on $R[s]$ is injective by comparison of polynomial coefficients. Thus $D$ is effective Cartier, also after every $R\to R'$. Its dual ideal [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle] has bases $e_0=1$, $e_1=s^{-1}$ with $e_0=s e_1=(x_0/x_1)e_1$, so it is exactly $\mathcal O_P(1)$ [def-pc-projective-space-twist]. These formulas also show that the infinity section and this line bundle pull back to their counterparts on $P'$.

Work first on the ordinary etale sites and put $A=\mathbf Z/N\mathbf Z$. For $B=A$ or $\Lambda$, put $L_{T,B}=B_{T,\mathrm{et}}(1)$ and define
$$b_{S,B}:L_{S,B}[2]\oplus B_S\longrightarrow Rp_{\mathrm{et},*}L_{P,B}[2].$$
Its first component is the shifted unit $L_{S,B}[2]\to Rp_*p^{-1}L_{S,B}[2]$, using twist pullback; its second component is adjoint to the scalar-extended Kummer class of $\mathcal O_P(1)$ [def-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-kummer-class]. For arbitrary $g:S'\to S$, these two components commute with the canonical exchange. For the unit this is the adjunction triangle identity in the three-factor exchange formula [def-kun-unbounded-exchange]. For the class, pullback of units gives a morphism from the inverse image of the Kummer sequence to the Kummer sequence on $P'$ [lem-amb-kummer-any-base]; the map on kernels is the root comparison of [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. The frame torsor of $\mathcal O(1)$ [lem-sc-line-bundle-torsor] pulls back to the frame torsor of the line bundle with the same transition functions from step 1. Naturality of torsor classes and connecting maps [lem-amb-relative-torsor-cohomology], with empty open complement, therefore sends its Kummer boundary to the boundary on $P'$. Applying the adjunction-mate formula gives
$$\operatorname{BC}_{g,B}\,g^{-1}b_{S,B}=b_{S',B}\,e_{g,B},$$
where $e_{g,B}$ is the ordered-sum comparison for $L_{S,B}[2]\oplus B_S$.

For $B=A$, the finite-coefficient geometric-fibre formula [cor-weil-pbc-geometric-fiber-finite] identifies its cohomology stalks with the shifted cohomology of $\mathbf P^1_{\bar s}$. Apply derived geometric-stalk conservativity [lem-weil-pbc-derived-stalk-conservative] to the underlying abelian complexes (a map of coefficient modules is invertible whenever its underlying map is). These complexes are bounded below since they are derived direct images of shifted sheaves. The fibre is a smooth proper connected genus-zero curve by [lem-asd-projective-line-genus-zero]. Choose a primitive $N$th root only for this fibre calculation. Then [thm-sc-proper-cohomology] gives $H^0=A$, $H^1=0$, $H^2=A$ under root trivialization, and zero cohomology above degree two. Applying [lem-sc-constant-proper-degree-coordinates] with the identical algebraically closed fields and the curve itself as compactification identifies the Kummer boundary of a line bundle with its degree modulo $N$. By step 1 and [lem-pc-degree-agrees-sc], $\mathcal O(1)=\mathcal O([\infty])$ has degree $1$. Thus the two components of $b_{S,A}$ induce isomorphisms on the only nonzero cohomology groups (degrees $-2,0$ after the shift), so $b_{S,A}$ is an isomorphism.

For general finite $\Lambda$, apply derived scalar extension $-\otimes_A^L\Lambda_S$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] to this isomorphism. The proper projection formula [lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection], with coefficient ring $A$, $K=\Lambda_S$ and $L=L_{P,A}[2]$, identifies its target with $Rp_*L_{P,\Lambda}[2]$. The identification of coefficient-restricted $Rp_*L_{P,\Lambda}$ with the direct image computed in $A$-modules follows from [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition]: apply its canonical composition comparison to $p$ and the identity-topos coefficient-restriction maps; restriction is exact, so its derived functor is restriction itself. Because the twist is a locally free $A$-line, $L_{P,A}\otimes_A^L\Lambda_P=L_{P,\Lambda}$. To specify the $\Lambda$-linear map, take the $p_\Lambda^{-1}\dashv Rp_{\Lambda,*}$-adjunct of $1\otimes\varepsilon_{p,L}$ from $p_\Lambda^{-1}(\Lambda_S\otimes_A^L Rp_{A,*}L)\cong\Lambda_P\otimes_A^L p_A^{-1}Rp_{A,*}L$ to $\Lambda_P\otimes_A^L L$, using the derived pullback tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. After restriction to $A$ this is precisely the canonical projection map, by its mate-of-counit definition. Hence it is invertible: exact restriction of coefficients detects zero cohomology and therefore reflects isomorphisms. The mate-of-counit definition of projection sends the unit component to the unit component and the Kummer component to its scalar extension, which is exactly the defining scalar-root map $z\mapsto1\otimes z$. Consequently the resulting map is $b_{S,\Lambda}$. This proves its invertibility even when $\Lambda$ is nonflat over $A$. The componentwise exchange equality above already proves its compatibility with every Noetherian base change. Write $b_S=b_{S,\Lambda}$ from now on.

proof.text:
Let $R_S=Rp_{\mathrm{et},*}\Lambda_P$ and $L_S=\Lambda_{S,\mathrm{et}}(1)$. The proper projection formula [lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection] and $p^{-1}L_S\cong L_P$ identify the target of $b_S$ with $(R_S\otimes_\Lambda^L L_S)[2]$. Tensor $b_S$ with $L_S^\vee[-2]$ and use the evaluation $L_S\otimes L_S^\vee\cong\Lambda_S$ to obtain
$$F_S:\Lambda_S\oplus\Lambda_{S,\mathrm{et}}(-1)[-2]\xrightarrow{\sim}R_S.$$
The first component is the unit; the second is the adjoint form of the same Kummer class. These identifications commute with base change: twist pullback and evaluation do so by [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback], and exchange commutes with the projection map by the explicit two-composite equality of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence]. Consequently, writing $d_g:g^{-1}(\Lambda_S\oplus\Lambda_S(-1)[-2])\cong\Lambda_{S'}\oplus\Lambda_{S'}(-1)[-2]$, we have $\mathrm{BC}^{\mathrm{et}}_g\,g^{-1}F_S=F_{S'}d_g$. No flatness of $\Lambda$ over $\mathbf Z/\ell^r$ is needed: the invertible lines are flat over $\Lambda$ itself.

proof.text:
Apply $
u_S^*$ to $F_S$. This is an exact functor on complexes by [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact]; its canonical derived tensor comparison is an isomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. The bounded-below comparison is fully faithful by [sk-prop-sf-comparison]. All objects here are bounded below: the etale decomposition identifies $R_S$ with a sum in degrees $0,2$, and the coefficient sheaves and twists start in degree zero. For the qcqs map $p$, [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison] gives the canonical isomorphism
$$C_p:
u_S^*Rp_{\mathrm{et},*}\Lambda_P\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp_{\mathrm{proet},*}\Lambda_P.$$
Hence $\widetilde F_S=C_p\,
u_S^*F_S$ is an isomorphism with the source in (G2). Compatibility of $C_p$ with adjunction units identifies its first component with the pro-etale unit. For the second, the Chern class was defined by pulling back the same Kummer boundary. Its identification with the Cartier convention is precisely [sk-lem-geo-cartier]: the Cartier composite is $c_1(\mathcal O(D))$, for $D$ the infinity section and $\mathcal O(D)=\mathcal O_P(1)$. The polynomial and transition calculation in step 1 establishes the Cartier hypothesis for every base change and identifies $\mathcal O(D)$ with the specified $\mathcal O(1)$, including its sign. Thus (G2) is the stated map.

proof.text:
Check the exchange morphism itself. Let $g:S'\to S$ and $g_P:P'\to P$ be its projective-line base change. Write $a_g:g_{\mathrm{proet}}^*\nu_S^*\cong\nu_{S'}^*g_{\mathrm{et}}^*$ for the pullback comparison of [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison]. Under these identifications,
$$\mathrm{BC}^{\mathrm{proet}}_g\,g^*C_p
=C_{p'}\,\nu_{S'}^*(\mathrm{BC}^{\mathrm{et}}_g)\,a_g,$$
with the analogous pullback comparison on $P'$ understood. Indeed exchange is unit, followed by the pullback-square isomorphism, followed by the image of the counit, as explicitly given by [def-kun-unbounded-exchange]; the same adjunction-mate formula applies on the pro-etale sites using [sk-def-sfb-finite-derived-functors]. To spell out the substitution, for either proper projection $u:U\to V$ ($u=p$ or $p'$) write $H_T=\nu_T^*$, put hats on the pro-etale adjunction, and set $a_u:\widehat u^*H_V\cong H_Uu^*$. The unit and counit compatibility in [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison] are the two identities
$$\widehat\eta_{u,H_VK}=R\widehat u_*(a_{u,K}^{-1})\,C_{u,u^*K}\,H_V(\eta_{u,K}),\qquad
\widehat\varepsilon_{u,H_UE}\,\widehat u^*(C_{u,E})=H_U(\varepsilon_{u,E})\,a_{u,Ru_*E}.$$
In the three-factor formula $\mathrm{BC}^{\mathrm{et}}_{g,E}=Rp'_*g_P^*(\varepsilon_{p,E})\,Rp'_*(\theta_{Rp_*E})\,\eta_{p',g^*Rp_*E}$, the first identity replaces the unit factor and the second replaces the counit factor. Naturality moves $C$ past each intervening morphism. Compatibility of $a_u$ with composition identifies the middle factor with $\widehat\theta$ for the same square $pg_P=gp'$. The resulting three factors are exactly $R\widehat p'_*\widehat g_P^*(\widehat\varepsilon_{p,H_PE})\,R\widehat p'_*(\widehat\theta_{R\widehat p_*H_PE})\,\widehat\eta_{p',\widehat g^*R\widehat p_*H_PE}$, the pro-etale exchange at $H_PE$. Take $E=\Lambda_P$ to obtain the displayed comparison equation. Substitute the equality for $F_S$ from step 3 to obtain
$$\mathrm{BC}^{\mathrm{proet}}_g\,g^*\widetilde F_S=\widetilde F_{S'}d_g.$$
This proves the asserted compatibility with the canonical base-change map. Both decompositions and $d_g$ are invertible, so this equality also proves that this base-change map is an isomorphism on the coefficient object. Apply the same comparison equation also to the bounded-below input $\Lambda_P(1)[2]$. To identify it with twisting (G2), express the projection map as the mate of counit tensor identity. The displayed counit identity, together with the tensor comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], identifies its image under $\nu^*$ with the pro-etale projection map. Twist/exchange compatibility is the equality of the two composites in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence], now on the pro-etale ringed topoi. Consequently
$$B_S=C_{p,\Lambda_P(1)[2]}\nu_S^*b_S:\Lambda_S(1)[2]\oplus\Lambda_S\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp_*\Lambda_P(1)[2]$$
is precisely the twist of (G2), and satisfies $\operatorname{BC}^{(1)[2]}_g\,g^*B_S=B_{S'}e_g$, with $e_g$ the ordered-sum twist comparison.

proof.text:
Use $B_S$ and its base-change square from step 5. Define $\operatorname{Tr}_p=\operatorname{pr}_2B_S^{-1}$, exactly the projection specified in (G3). Multiplying that equality by the inverses and then projecting yields
$$\operatorname{Tr}_{p'}\,\mathrm{BC}^{(1)[2]}_g
=\operatorname{pr}_2e_g\,g^*(B_S^{-1})
=g^*(\operatorname{pr}_2B_S^{-1})=g^*\operatorname{Tr}_p.$$
The second equality uses that $e_g$ preserves the ordered summands and is the identity on the second coefficient summand. This is the required trace compatibility for every Noetherian base change. This last step is just inversion and composition of the preceding commutative square, not an additional trace theorem.
